s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with severe sore throat, neck pain, and neurological symptoms
salient_findings: High-grade fever
Pharyngeal erythema with enlarged tonsils and whitish tonsillar exudates
Stiff neck
Altered consciousness and generalized tonic-clonic seizures
CSF analysis showing leukocyte count of 250 cells/mm3
Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement on CT head/neck
Positive viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM
key_facts: Enlarged tonsils with whitish tonsillar exudates
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly on palpation
Altered consciousness and generalized tonic-clonic seizures
Post-ictal drowsiness and unresponsiveness to verbal commands

shortlist.label: Epstein-Barr virus encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive EBV DNA in CSF and clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Infectious mononucleosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM and clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and fatigue

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe neurological symptoms, including altered consciousness and seizures, which are consistent with HSV encephalitis

shortlist.label: Enteroviral meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: CSF analysis showing leukocyte count of 250 cells/mm3 and clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and neck pain

shortlist.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and neurological symptoms, including altered consciousness and seizures, which can be seen in ADEM

raw.rationale: The presence of positive viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM, absent Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen (EBNA), and positive EBV DNA in CSF strongly supports this diagnosis, as these are indicative of an acute EBV infection involving the central nervous system.

rejected.label: Infectious mononucleosis
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms consistent with infectious mononucleosis, such as fever and sore throat, the presence of altered consciousness, seizures, and specific CSF findings point more towards encephalitis.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of specific tests (like PCR) for HSV in the CSF, and the clinical presentation combined with the positive EBV markers makes this less likely.

rejected.label: Enteroviral meningitis
rejected.why: The CSF analysis shows a high number of leukocytes, but the presence of EBV DNA in CSF and the clinical presentation are more consistent with encephalitis due to EBV than enteroviral meningitis.

rejected.label: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: This is an autoimmune condition typically following a viral infection, but the direct evidence of EBV infection in the CSF makes it less likely compared to EBV encephalitis.
